classification: Authored educational scenarios. Resource rates, events, equipment, exposure and probabilities are illustrative; no measured NASA emergency data.

moon.title: Haven: the first watch
moon.brief: Stabilize a Mare Tranquillitatis outpost, protect four crewmates, repair a field relay, and return a basalt sample. Your seven decisions must leave the crew able to survive four hours until resupply.
moon.skill: Outpost operations, EVA planning and resource trade-offs

stages.title: Restore Haven’s distribution bus
stages.description: The damaged bus is isolating the array. Reconnect the wires, then decide how to distribute the restored supply.

options.label: Protect life support; dim the greenhouse
options.explanation: A smaller harvest protects oxygen production and the battery reserve.

options.label: Grow extra food now
options.explanation: Extra food uses water and power. Watch the battery forecast.

options.label: Use the reserve and bypass the array
options.explanation: Quick to restore, but the outpost stays dependent on stored energy.

stages.title: Seal a slow habitat leak
stages.description: Inspect the airlock seals. A leak is using oxygen that the crew will need until resupply.

options.label: Fit a replacement gasket
options.explanation: A maintenance kit repairs the leak and improves habitat condition.

options.label: Isolate the workshop
options.explanation: Closing a module saves oxygen but reduces available laboratory space.

options.label: Flush the module and defer the repair
options.explanation: The leak continues. Flushing wastes oxygen and does not repair the gasket.

stages.title: Respond to a radiation training alert
stages.description: A fictional solar-particle alert has arrived. Choose protection before the EVA. These dose rates are game assumptions.

options.label: Move supplies into passive shelter walls
options.explanation: Stored material adds shielding without continuous electrical demand.

options.label: Use the experimental powered shield
options.explanation: An experimental teaching concept: uses extra power to reduce modelled exposure. This is not flight-ready protection; passive shelter is the established strategy in this exercise.

options.label: Continue without extra shielding
options.explanation: The crew is more exposed during the alert; health and the EVA envelope decline.

stages.title: Prepare and release the EVA
stages.description: Check the suit, seal the inner hatch, vent, and open the outer hatch. Then choose a field load.

options.label: Take the light science kit
options.explanation: The light load preserves walking speed and suit reserves.

options.label: Carry the expanded instrument pack
options.explanation: More instruments improve science but consume more oxygen and crew energy.

options.label: Carry extra emergency oxygen
options.explanation: Transferred outpost oxygen extends the suit reserve; it is not free oxygen.

stages.title: Repair the field relay
stages.description: Reach the orange relay and reconnect its signal circuit. Your suit, return route, and exposure continue to matter.

options.label: Fit a tested spare board
options.explanation: A reliable repair uses a maintenance kit.

options.label: Calibrate the damaged board
options.explanation: Saves the spare, but the longer EVA uses oxygen and battery.

options.label: Install a temporary bypass
options.explanation: Quick to connect, but the bypass costs energy and reduces reliability.

stages.title: Collect and document a basalt sample
stages.description: Walk to the cyan field marker. Use the scan and sample tools, then choose the scope of the observation.

options.label: Tag and seal one representative sample
options.explanation: A focused observation records location and conserves EVA time.

options.label: Run the full instrument survey
options.explanation: More science costs time, battery, and crew energy.

options.label: Photograph the site and return early
options.explanation: The crew uses fewer reserves, but the science goal may remain unmet.

stages.title: Return, stow the sample, and secure Haven
stages.description: Return to the white Haven marker. Stow the sample and select the operating plan that must last until resupply.

options.label: Turn off extra loads; replenish the suit
options.explanation: Essential loads and passive protection preserve the remaining resources. Transfer 30 nominal oxygen minutes and 20 Wh from Haven to the suit.

options.label: Use the experimental powered shield
options.explanation: An experimental teaching concept: uses extra power to reduce modelled exposure. This is not flight-ready protection; passive shelter is the established strategy in this exercise.

options.label: Spend the emergency fuel on the backup generator
options.explanation: The backup adds 2 kW but consumes the finite emergency reserve.

mars.title: Jezero: hold the line
mars.brief: Keep a Jezero outpost supplied through a dust advisory, repair communications, and return a sediment sample. Protect the four-person crew and leave four hours of reserves for resupply.
mars.skill: Dust response, life support and surface science

stages.title: Restore Jezero’s dusty power bus
stages.description: Reconnect the distribution bus. Dust is reducing solar supply; choose essential loads before sending the crew outside.

stages.title: Respond to a dust advisory
stages.description: A restrained fictional dust front is approaching. Decide how to protect power and air filtration.

options.label: Brush the panels and protect the air filter
options.explanation: Cleaning improves generation and protects the habitat; it uses a service kit.

options.label: Deploy backup power
options.explanation: A 2 kW generator supports essentials while dust reduces array output.

options.label: Wait out the dust without maintenance
options.explanation: The array stays dusty. Check the energy deficit before the EVA.
